refuter_findings.evidence: The cited `thm-morse-trajectory-compactness-up-to-breaking` treats sequences in `M(p,q)` with fixed critical endpoints. Proof 3.1 applies it to tails cut at `-S`, whose endpoint `u_n(-S)` varies and is generally noncritical, so those tails are not in the cited moduli space. Proof 6.1 also asserts a height path for the time-dependent middle, although the energy identity gives `d/ds f_s(u) = -|u'|² + ∂_s f_s(u)`, which need not be monotone; `def-broken-continuation-trajectory` instead uses compact-time tests on the middle and transversal tests on the tails. Finally, F7/Proof 7.1 promotes separate half-line right inverses to uniform whole-line inverses for neck operators. The cited half-line lemma only gives an inverse for an individual half-line operator, and the cited Banach IFT requires an exact zero and an invertible partial derivative. These do not establish the claimed extraction, compactification, or density.

The cited Banach IFT requires `F(a,b)=0` and an invertible partial derivative. Here `w_T` is an approximate curve with nonzero defect, and the proof supplies only a right inverse, with no kernel slice or complementary isomorphism; for an index-one surjective operator the kernel is nonzero. The cited half-line operator lemma provides separate right inverses, not a uniform inverse estimate for the neck-dependent whole-line operators. Thus the IFT does not produce the asserted unique, smooth family or eventual containment.

F2 asserts a canonical orientation of the continuation Fredholm determinant line, and F3 assumes a determinant-line gluing isomorphism. The cited `def-fredholm-maps-and-regular-values-on-countable-banach-manifolds` defines Fredholm index and regular values; `def-determinant-line-orientation-of-a-finite-dimensional-real-vector-space` only defines orientations for finite-dimensional spaces. The cited continuation gluing lemma establishes neither a determinant-line identification nor a gluing isomorphism. Consequently the induced orientations and the two displayed boundary signs are not established.

The proof says, “Over Z/2 every determinant line has a unique trivialization.” The cited determinant-line definition says a real determinant line has two orientation rays, including in dimension zero. Mod-two counts discard signs; they do not choose a unique trivialization of those real lines.

refuter_findings.location: Facts F1 and F3; Statement K; Proof 1.1–3.1
refuter_findings.evidence: F1 asserts compactness, finiteness, collars, and a boundary formula for the augmented `(λ,u)` moduli space. But the current `def-two-parameter-continuation-homotopy` explicitly says parameterized compactness, gluing, and orientation are separate requirements “not supplied” by regularity. The fixed-datum compactness theorem also requires a regular member, whereas a rogue trajectory has a non-surjective fixed-parameter operator. No augmented compactness, gluing, or boundary-sign argument licenses the count defining K or the displayed identity.

F2 claims a gluing bijection for two rigid continuation solutions. The cited `lem-gluing-continuation-solutions-gives-collar-ends` states only the cases `(γ⁻,v)` and `(v,γ⁺)`, each joining an autonomous Morse tail to a continuation solution. It supplies no continuation–continuation gluing, neck-dependent regularity, exhaustion of solutions, or signed compatibility, so it does not license the asserted bijection or chain-level equality.

The cited `thm-index-two-compactification-is-a-compact-one-manifold-with-boundary` assumes index drop two and establishes a one-dimensional trajectory compactification; its collar lemma covers once-broken index-two trajectories. These do not construct compactified unstable disks in all dimensions or the relative boundary-exit extension asserted here. The cited `lem-a-handle-decomposition-gives-a-relative-cw-complex` supplies a CW model of the pair with one cell per handle, not an identification with the actual compactified unstable manifolds. Proof 2.2 also infers that the exit stratum is closed merely from continuity of exit points, without controlling limits that break at a critical point before exiting.

Proof 3.1 says the value filtration coincides with the increasing-index filtration. Excellence only requires distinct critical values. For example, on the disjoint union of two circles take `cos(θ)` on one component and `100 + cos(θ)` on the other. This is Morse–Smale and excellent, but an index-one maximum at value 1 occurs below an index-zero minimum at value 99. The claimed filtrations therefore need not coincide.

The proof takes the compactified continuation space to be a compact one-manifold with the stated boundary, then uses its signed boundary count. Its cited compactness proof does not establish compactness for moving tail endpoints or the augmented extraction, and its cited gluing proof applies the Banach IFT to a nonzero approximate curve without an invertible slice. The orientation lemma cited by F3 also assumes the determinant-line gluing isomorphism rather than proving it. Thus the compact oriented one-manifold and its signed boundary formula are not established by the cited dependencies.

Proof 2.1 constructs an isomorphism for a fixed Morse–Smale pair. Proof 4.1 then invokes continuation isomorphisms, their inverses, and their composition law to claim independence of the pair, but provides no comparison showing `θ_(f1,X1) ∘ Φ = θ_(f0,X0)`. Existence of continuation isomorphisms does not imply compatibility with the separately constructed cellular comparisons; the claimed choice-independence is therefore not proved.

F1 says regularity is generic “on the path of metrics with fixed ends.” The cited `def-regular-continuation-datum-between-morse-smale-pairs` says genericity varies both `f_s` and `g_s` and explicitly warns that metric variations alone can fail when a point remains critical throughout the function path. The citation does not support the metric-only claim.

reader_findings.evidence: The autonomous compactness supplier concerns full trajectories with fixed critical endpoints, whereas the tails cut at ±S have varying noncritical endpoints. Extraction of the intervening critical chain is not proved. Step 6.1 asserts a continuous height-path encoding without defining its domains or proving an inverse; the middle solution is not height-monotone, and declaring the broken locus closed does not follow from the stated extraction. F7 incorrectly treats compactly supported perturbations and separate half-line right inverses as giving surjectivity and uniform whole-line inverse bounds. Supply variable-endpoint tail compactness, a valid topological encoding, and uniform multi-neck gluing estimates. The current batch-5 compactness supplier also restricts to normalized gradient-like fields, while this item permits arbitrary metric-gradient ends.

Local evolution and individual half-line right inverses do not prove a uniformly bounded inverse for the neck-dependent whole-line operator. An open-condition argument at each fixed operator does not provide a uniform bound as neck length diverges. The invoked implicit-function theorem requires an exact zero and an invertible partial derivative; the approximate curve is not a zero, and the index-one operator has a kernel. A complement/slice, quantitative contraction estimate, and nonlinear derivative control are missing. Uniqueness on that slice cannot establish injectivity and eventual containment until a neck coordinate and nearby-solution decomposition are proved. Supply that gluing argument, keeping the time-dependent middle solution unshifted, and smooth collars sufficient for the later smooth boundary-count suppliers.

Surjectivity alone does not orient a determinant-line bundle. F2 assumes the desired canonical asymptotic identification, and F3 assumes the determinant-line gluing isomorphism; the finite-dimensional determinant definition and the topological collar lemma establish neither. Separate one-sided collars do not represent the negative and positive ends of one common interval, so the claimed relative boundary signs do not follow from the interval convention. Supply a transverse endpoint exact-sequence orientation and an actual negative-tail versus positive-tail tangent/determinant comparison, or a complete coherent-orientation gluing theorem with these conventions. Step 4.1 additionally falsely says that real determinant lines have a unique trivialization over mod-two coefficients; dropping counting signs does not trivialize those real lines.

reader_findings.location: Facts F1 and F3; Statement K; Proof 1.1–3.1 (lines 39–54, 61–93, 107–113)
reader_findings.evidence: The cited compactness and collar theorems require a regular fixed continuation datum; a rogue trajectory has vertical index -1 and its fixed-datum linearization cannot be surjective. Those theorems therefore cannot establish compactness, finiteness, collars or orientations for the augmented (lambda,u) problem. The repaired two-parameter definition supplies augmented regularity and dimension, not these further assertions. Supply uniform parameter-dependent compactness, augmented gluing (allowing lambda to change), and its oriented boundary formula, including endpoint signs, before counting K and deriving the integral chain-homotopy identity. F3 only names product signs and does not establish the displayed minus signs in the boundary sum. Its final consequence also calls the chain-map supplier an isomorphism theorem, although that supplier establishes only a homomorphism; invertibility is proved later and must not be attributed to it.

The cited collar lemma glues one autonomous Morse tail to one continuation solution at total index drop one. Here two rigid continuation solutions are glued at total index difference zero while the spliced datum itself changes with neck length. No such bijection, regularity of all resulting rigid solutions, exhaustion of solutions as the neck diverges, or signed compatibility is supplied. Counting a bijection without orientation compatibility also does not give the integral composite. Supply a continuation–continuation gluing theorem and its signs (the distinct case described in Fowdar Theorem 6.11, rather than the autonomous-tail case), plus control of any small perturbation before asserting chain-level equality.

The fixed-end trajectory compactness and index-two collars do not construct compactified unstable disks in all dimensions or prove the relative boundary-exit extension. Audin–Damian Section 4.9 proves the closed case by a separate variable-endpoint construction, not by iterating index-two collars; its relative extension is not supplied here. Step 2.2 wrongly declares the unbroken exit stratum closed: exit trajectories may converge to a critical break followed by exit. Step 3.1 falsely identifies value filtration with index filtration; an excellent Morse function need not order critical values by index. The handle supplier gives only a relative CW homotopy model and explicitly does not assert a global unstable closure. Supply the relative unstable-disk construction and its comparison with handles; do not identify these filtrations without a rearrangement argument.

The proof produces an isomorphism for a fixed pair but does not prove theta_(f1,X1) composed with the continuation map equals theta_(f0,X0). Existence, inverse and composition laws for continuation isomorphisms do not imply this compatibility with independently constructed cellular comparisons. Step 3.1 also asserts without a construction that all CW auxiliary changes give an isomorphism through which Theta factors. Supply the comparison-versus-continuation commutative diagram via a parametrized unstable-chain/cellular homotopy, and its orientation normalization; an abstract isomorphism of groups alone does not establish the stated choice-independence.

reader_findings.location: Pre-reader Proof 2.1, fixed critical-string extraction and passage to the height ODE
reader_findings.evidence: The observed proof passed to a constant string of already present break points and then passed the height ODE on each entire intervening interval. Split at every critical point actually met by the limiting height graph. The producer has since replaced this proof; the pre hash binds the old argument actually read.
